requirements.quote: **No runtime dependencies.** `package.json` may have `devDependencies` only; the shipped game is your own code.

opening `dist/index.html` straight from disk (double-clicked, a `file://` address, no server at all) gives a playable game. A browser refuses to load separate script or style files for a page opened that way, so they belong inside the page.
The built site must also work from **any path** on a static server — at `/` and at a sub-path such as `/games/minesweeper/` — so any asset URLs are relative.
Pure logic: no DOM, no timers, no `Math.random` except as described for `seed`.
**Immutable.** No function changes the `Game` it is given. A call that changes nothing returns the very same object it was given.
`rows` and `cols` are integers from 5 to 50, and `mines` from 1 to `rows × cols − 9`. Anything else makes `createGame` throw a `RangeError`.
With `layout`, the board is exactly that grid: `rows`, `cols` and `mines` come from it (any given are ignored), mines never move, and `adjacent` is set from the start. The size rule still applies.

Without `layout`, mines are placed at the first `reveal`: exactly `mines` of them, never on the revealed cell or any of its neighbours. With a `seed`, the placement depends only on the seed, the board size and the first cell.
Until placement every cell has `adjacent: 0` and `mine: false`.

`ready` until the first reveal, then `playing`; `lost` when a mine is revealed; `won` when every non-mine cell is revealed (flags are not needed). Once `won` or `lost`, every function returns the game unchanged.

Revealing a hidden, unflagged cell reveals it. If it has `adjacent: 0`, its neighbours are revealed too, and so on outward: the connected region of zero cells and the numbered cells bordering it (8-neighbour connectivity). Flagged cells are never revealed this way.

`lastRevealed` lists every cell the call revealed, each with its `distance`: 0 for the clicked cell, otherwise the fewest steps from the clicked cell to it, moving one neighbour at a time and passing only through revealed zero cells.
Revealing a revealed or flagged cell changes nothing.
**Loss.** Revealing a mine reveals every mine, and the game is `lost`. Flags stay where they are.
**Win.** When the game is `won`, every mine is flagged.
`toggleFlag` flags or unflags a hidden cell; on a revealed cell it changes nothing. There may be more flags than mines.

`chord` on a revealed cell whose number equals the count of flagged neighbours reveals every hidden, unflagged neighbour, exactly as `reveal` would (flood included, and a wrong flag can lose the game). `lastRevealed` measures `distance` from the chorded cell, which is 0 but not itself newly revealed. Otherwise `chord` changes nothing.
`minesLeft` is `mines` minus the number of flagged cells; it can be negative.
**Mouse:** left click reveals; right click toggles a flag (no browser menu appears); left click on a revealed number chords.

**Keyboard:** the board is one Tab stop — exactly one cell has `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`. Arrow keys move focus between cells and stop at the edges. Enter or Space reveals the focused cell, or chords it if it is a revealed number; `F` toggles its flag. Focus is always visible.
**State is immediate.** Cell `data-state`, `#mines-left`, `#status` and the rest change in the same task as the input that changed them — never after an animation.
**Best times** are kept per board: per difficulty, and per `?board` value. A win is recorded when it beats the stored time.

`?board=` fixes the board: rows separated by `,`, each a string of `*` (mine) and `.` (safe) — `?board=*....,.....,.....,.....,.....`. The game uses that layout (rule 3), and `#new-game` starts it again.
`?seed=` with an integer makes a random game repeatable (rule 4), at the current difficulty.
With neither, the board is random at the remembered difficulty (beginner the first time).
Every sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API — no audio files.
requirements.not_tested: Sound synthesis via Web Audio API is verified by code review (OscillatorNode usage, no audio files) in the page implementation task and by the R44/R45 e2e tests (no AudioContext before first gesture, muted = silent); the actual audible output of each distinct sound is not testable headlessly.

requirements.quote: Distinct sounds for: revealing one cell, a cascade (one reveal that opens more than one cell), placing a flag, removing a flag, a chord, an explosion (loss), and a win — the win is a short melody of at least three notes.
requirements.not_tested: Distinct sounds per event are verified structurally (code review confirms separate synth paths per event type and a ≥3-note win melody); headless Playwright cannot assert on audible frequency/timbre distinctions.

requirements.quote: **Reveal ripple.** Every newly revealed cell animates in (100–600 ms), starting `distance × step` after the input, with a fixed step of 15–40 ms, so a cascade ripples outward from the click. No cell starts later than 1000 ms after the input.
**Flag.** Placing a flag animates.
**Loss.** The exploded mine animates (a flash, a shake), and the other mines appear one after another rather than all at once.
**Win.** The board or the status celebrates.
**Reduced motion.** When the user prefers reduced motion, nothing animates and nothing transitions: no CSS animations, no CSS transitions, no Web Animations.
